sections.heading: Silicone Restoration vs. Full Roof Replacement on East Orange Flat Roofs

c.v: Coat when the roof is sound underneath and only the surface has worn out; choose a full roof replacement when water has reached the insulation or the deck.

runs.v: A coating candidate has a structurally sound deck, dry insulation, and a weathered but attached membrane, whether modified bitumen, EPDM, TPO, built-up, metal, or spray polyurethane foam, and the liquid-applied membrane bonds over each one after the leaks at seams and flashings are repaired. Coating over wet insulation only seals the water in, so a roof with saturated insulation needs a tear off and a new roof instead.

Where the roof qualifies, a professionally applied coating typically saves 50 to 70% of the cost of a full replacement, most coating jobs are finished in 1 to 3 days, and the building stays occupied, which matters on a rental block where a full tear off means weeks of noise and debris above tenants. A silicone coating system can extend roof life by 10 to 20 years before the next recoat, and a commercial coating is typically classified as maintenance rather than a capital improvement, per the RCMA, a tax question for the owner's accountant. Silicone is a flat and low-slope product, ideal for flat roofs with drainage issues: it is not used on pitched roofs covered with shingles, which need shingle repair or replacement.

sections.heading: What Are the Downsides of Using Silicone Roof Coating?

c.v: Silicone coatings have trade-offs worth knowing before a free roofing estimate.

runs.v: Silicone costs more per square foot than acrylic, and while its water-shedding surface resists mold, it holds airborne dirt, so reflectance falls as the surface ages; it is also slippery when wet. Only silicone sticks to cured silicone, so every future recoat is silicone. It will not fix a roof with wet insulation or a failed deck, and it cannot be applied to a damp surface. For most ponding-prone East Orange flat roofs those limits are acceptable; for a roof past saving, the money belongs in a new roof.

faqs.q: Does silicone roof coating hold up in ponding water on my East Orange apartment building?

A 100% silicone roof coating resists permanent and standing water without softening or losing adhesion, while water-based acrylic re-emulsifies under continuous immersion and most acrylic warranties exclude ponded areas, per the RCMA, Gaco, and Western Colloid. The roof is still cleaned and dried before coating, because even ponding-resistant silicone needs a clean dry surface.

faqs.q: How long does a silicone roof coating last on an East Orange building?

runs.v: A silicone roof coating carries a renewable 10, 15, or 20 year manufacturer warranty, with the term scaling to dry-film thickness, per the RCMA, Henry, Mule-Hide, and Gaco. A maintained silicone roof is recoated with silicone at the end of the term rather than torn off, which extends service life on East Orange's pre-war flat roofs at a fraction of replacement cost.

faqs.q: Does a reflective silicone coating lower energy costs on an East Orange top-floor apartment?

runs.v: It can lower energy costs in summer: a reflective roof stays more than 50°F cooler than a conventional roof on a sunny afternoon, per the DOE, and cuts peak cooling demand by 11 to 27% in air-conditioned residential buildings, per the EPA, a peak-demand figure rather than an annual bill. The coating adds no meaningful R-value, so the net annual benefit is smaller in East Orange's heating-dominated Climate Zone 4 to 5, per the RCMA and DOE.

faqs.q: Can silicone coating be recoated with acrylic later?

runs.v: No. Cured silicone is recoated with silicone, not with acrylic or urethane, because coatings adhere to silicone only as silicone, and switching away from silicone generally requires removal first, per Gaco and the RCMA. A silicone roof recoats over silicone after cleaning, which keeps each renewal simpler than the original application.
